0.content:
[Homunculus manual: map of the app]
Homunculus is a personal fork of SillyTavern (through SillyBunny) with its own interface, Agents, Group Studio, Scene panel and Vault. The interface is in English.
Where things are (names as they appear on screen):
- Home: start screen with recent chats, characters, lorebooks and your persona.
- Chat: the open conversation.
- Characters: your character cards; open one to chat or edit it.
- Group Studio: create and set up group chats (cast, narrator, your role, Scene panel, agents, settings).
- Vault: reusable Scenarios and NPCs.
- Lorebooks: World Info entries the AI reads when keywords appear.
- Persona: who you are in the story ({{user}}).
- Agents: helpers that run before or after each reply, or track the scene.
- Memory: Chapters (summaries) and Recall (finding old messages).
- Card Browser: find and import character cards online.
- Presets: model settings and the prompt (Prompt Manager).
- API: connect to a model provider.
- Formatting, Extensions, Backgrounds, Customize (visual profiles, layout, effects), Settings.
Layouts: "Classic" puts icons in a top bar with drawers; "Lantern" puts a labeled sidebar on the left with one page at a time. Change it in Customize › Layout.
Most screens have small "?" buttons that explain each option.

1.content:
[Homunculus manual: connecting a model]
Nothing replies until a model is connected. "Not connected to API!" in the message box means no model is connected yet.
1. Open API (plug icon). Pick a Chat Completion source (for example OpenRouter, OpenAI, Claude, Google), paste the API key and press Connect.
2. Choose a model from the list.
3. Save it as a Connection Profile (in the same screen) so you can switch back to it later.
Quick Connection: the link (chain) button in the message box opens a small menu with your saved connection profiles on the left and that profile's models on the right. Picking one switches right away; a star pins a model to the top. It only shows profiles you saved first.

2.content:
[Homunculus manual: Home]
Home is the house icon. It shows a search box, a Continue button for your last chat, your recent chats, your characters, lorebooks and the persona you are playing as. The Blood & Ink profile uses a different Home style ("specimen") with the same content. Clicking a character or a recent chat opens it.

3.content:
[Homunculus manual: characters]
Characters holds your character cards. Click a card to open its chat. To edit it, open the character and use its editor.
The editor (Lantern layout) has a side column with the portrait, Chat and Lore buttons, numbered sections (Identity, First message, Who they are, Details) with a check when filled, and a token budget. On the right, "How it looks in the chat" previews the first message and gives tips (description too short, no alternate greeting, no dialogue examples).
Alternate greetings become swipes on the first message of a new chat.
Permanent tokens (description, personality, scenario) are sent with every message; fewer leaves more room for the story.
Import: the import button in Characters takes a card file (PNG/JSON) or a link; the Card Browser finds cards online.

4.content:
[Homunculus manual: Card Browser]
Card Browser (globe icon) searches character cards online and imports them without leaving the app. Sources: ChubAI, JannyAI, Wyvern, DataCat and Pygmalion (pick one at the top right). Search, sort (Most downloaded, Hot this week, Top rated...), Tags and Filters narrow the list; Show NSFW is a toggle. In Tags, tick a tag to require it or press "−" to hide cards with it. Open a card to read it and import it. If a site does not answer, the page says so with a Try again button.

5.content:
[Homunculus manual: chat basics]
Write in the message box and press Enter or the send button. Arrows on the last reply swipe to other versions (right arrow on the last one generates a new version). The pencil on a message edits it; the "…" menu holds more actions (delete, branch, and others). The buttons around the message box come from SillyTavern; hovering shows their names.

6.content:
[Homunculus manual: Group Studio]
Group Studio (group icon) creates and sets up group chats. The left list shows your groups; New group starts one.
A new group first asks "How do you want to play?":
- Simple group chat (standard SillyTavern): everyone replies in turn, you play your persona, no Scene panel.
- Narrated adventure (added by Homunculus): one narrator voices the whole cast and keeps track of the world; Scene panel on.
- Write a story together (added by Homunculus): you are the Director, nobody plays a character, the characters act on their own; Plot panel and Let them act / Auto-play.
- Start from scratch, or start from a scenario in the Vault.
The choice only fills in the Setup; everything stays editable. The footer "Ready to play" lists what is done and what is missing; click an item to go there.
Tabs: Setup (name, mode, narrator, how the story starts, your role, story style), Cast (members, In scene / Offscreen / Off, cast sheets), Scene (trackers for the Scene panel), Chats, Agents (agents for this group only), Settings (preset, persona, extra lorebooks, prompts, who replies).
Modes: Ensemble = everyone replies in turn. Narrated = only the narrator replies and voices everyone; the other members become cast sheets. The narrator can be one of your characters or a built-in narrator made for the group.
Unnamed groups get a name from the cast or the Vault scenario.

7.content:
[Homunculus manual: your role in the story]
Group Studio › Setup › Your role in the story:
- Player: you play {{user}}; your messages are what your character says and does.
- Co-author: {{user}} is in the story, but the AI writes them too; your messages are directions ("have them argue").
- Director: there is no {{user}} in the story; you direct from outside or just watch. You can pick a main character.
In Co-author and Director, your messages show as "direction" in the chat, and the group bar gets Let them act (one turn with no direction) and Auto-play ×3/5/10 (several turns; Stop ends it). "When I send nothing" chooses whether the characters act or the scene just continues.

8.content:
[Homunculus manual: the group bar]
Every group chat has a bar above the messages. Left: the group's avatars, name and a line like "Narrated · you play Kael"; click it to open Group Studio. Middle (Co-author and Director only): Let them act, Auto-play, Stop. Right: Group settings, Agents, Scene, "?" and "⋯" (Open Group Studio, Start a new chat, Chats of this group, Rename group).
Group settings: a group can bring its own preset, persona, lorebooks and agents. While its chat is open they replace your usual ones. The button says "Group settings on" or "Your own settings"; its panel lists what the group brings and has the switch "Use my own settings in this chat". Nothing in the group is lost when you switch it off. Change them in Group Studio › Settings.

9.content:
[Homunculus manual: Scene panel]
The Scene panel sits beside the chat and is filled by Scene trackers, agents that read each reply and update the state. Turn them on per group in Group Studio › Scene:
- Scene: World: time, place, weather, quests, items and the preset's own fields.
- Scene: Characters: who is here, what they look like, outfit, mood, traits.
- Scene: Plot: threads, what each character wants, secrets, and your planned beats.
Each tracker can use its own model (a cheap fast one is enough) and a field preset (Fields / Edit fields).
Panel tabs: Cast, Plot, Quests, Items, World. Everything in the panel can be edited by clicking it; the next update starts from your edit. Update now runs the trackers on the last message. Statuses (Brewing, Active, Done, Failed; Steer toward, Not yet) open a menu when clicked. Planned beats marked Steer toward pull the story there; Not yet holds them back.
Quests show for Player and Co-author; in Director there is no {{user}} to own them, so goals live in Plot.

10.content:
[Homunculus manual: Vault]
Vault (safe icon) keeps things you reuse across groups and chats.
- Scenarios: a setting, its NPCs, several first messages, a start time, lorebooks and tags. A scenario can start a new group, be used in the open chat, or be made from one of your characters (From a character).
- NPCs: full sheets (description, traits, stats, appearance, background, personality, speech, relationships, goals). Save them from the Scene panel or a scenario, fill the gaps with AI, add them to a scenario, or Turn into a character (a real card).
In Group Studio, Setup › How the story starts has Load from the Vault / Save to the Vault, and Cast has a From the Vault area for NPCs.

11.content:
[Homunculus manual: Agents]
Agents are small AI helpers attached to the chat. Some run before the reply (they add instructions), some after it (for example Prose Polisher rewrites tired wording), and trackers/companions run beside it (like the Scene trackers). Each agent can use its own connection profile and model.
The Agents screen (robot icon) lists them with an on/off switch; Templates has the built-in ones to install; New Agent makes your own; the pencil opens the editor with its prompt.
In a group chat, the Agents button on the group bar opens a menu for that group only: switch agents on or off just there, see what each one did on the last reply, run trackers now, or open their editor. Group Studio › Agents does the same.

12.content:
[Homunculus manual: Memory]
Memory (brain icon) has two tabs and works per chat (open a chat first):
- Chapters: several summaries, each covering a range of messages, written by the AI or by hand and switched on or off. Switched-on chapters go into the prompt where you choose (before or after the main prompt, inside the chat at a depth, or only where {{chapters}} is written). Summarized messages can be hidden from the AI to save room.
- Recall: finds old messages that look like the current moment and adds them to the prompt (it drives SillyTavern's Vector Storage).

13.content:
[Homunculus manual: Lorebooks]
Lorebooks (World Info) hold entries the AI reads only when their keywords appear in the recent chat, so world details do not cost tokens all the time. Open Lorebooks to create one, add entries (keywords + content) and choose which lorebooks are active. A character can have its own lorebook (the Lore button in the editor), and a group can add extra lorebooks in Group Studio › Settings.

14.content:
[Homunculus manual: Persona]
Your persona is who you are in the story: a name, a description and an avatar, used as {{user}}. Open Persona to create or switch personas. A persona can be locked to a chat or a character. A group can bring its own persona (Group Studio › Settings).

15.content:
[Homunculus manual: presets and prompts]
Presets (sliders icon) hold the model settings (context size, response length, temperature...) and the Prompt Manager, the list of blocks sent to the AI in order.
Homunculus adds its own blocks: Role instructions, Story style, The author's plan, Current scene and Cast sheets. They go where your preset has their section. In Group Studio › Settings › Prompts, a block marked "Not sent: no place in your preset" is not reaching the AI: press "Add them to my preset" and then save the preset. "See the last prompt" shows what was actually sent.
Story style (Group Studio › Setup) sets things like point of view, tense and length with simple choices; Edit options lets you change them or add your own.

16.content:
[Homunculus manual: Customize]
Customize (palette icon) changes how the app looks:
- Visual profile: Classic (uses the UI Theme from Settings, no effects), Arcane Lantern (night and gold, seven effects) and Blood & Ink (red, black and bone, with the "specimen" Home). You can import or export profiles.
- Layout: Classic (top icon bar, drawers over the chat) or Lantern (labeled sidebar, one page at a time; desktop only).
- Effects: each one can be switched on or off (Lantern light, Halo, Sheen, Stardust, Aurora, Blur-in, Glow, Watching eye), with intensity and an effect color.
Backgrounds (picture icon) changes the chat background.

17.content:
[Homunculus manual: updating and problems]
Updating: in the Homunculus folder, run git pull, then reload the page with Ctrl+F5. If an update added server parts, close the app and open it again (Start-Node.bat).
Common problems:
- Nothing replies: no model connected (see connecting a model).
- Group story instructions ignored: Group Studio › Settings › Prompts shows "Not sent: no place in your preset"; press "Add them to my preset" and save the preset.
- Scene panel empty: no tracker is on for the group (Group Studio › Scene), or it has not run yet (Update now).
- A setting seems wrong in one chat only: check the group bar; "Group settings on" means the group's own preset, persona or agents are in use.
